exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Cube Given a Side Length

question.text: Determine the surface area for the cube above.
question.explanation:
The surface area $S$ of a cube can be found using the formula

\[ S = 6s^2, \]

where $s$ is the side length of the cube.

Substituting $s = 2\sqrt{5}\,\textrm{cm}$ into the formula, we get \[ S = 6 (2\sqrt{5}\, \text{cm})^2 = 120\,\textrm{cm}^2 . \]

question.text: Find the surface area of the cube whose sides each have length $4\sqrt{7}\, \text{in}.$
question.explanation:
The surface area $S$ of a cube can be found using the formula

\[ S = 6s^2, \]

where $s$ is the side length of the cube.

Substituting $s = 4\sqrt{7}\,\textrm{in}$ into the formula, we get

\[ S = 6(4\sqrt{7}\, \text{in})^2 = 672 \,\textrm{in}^2 . \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Side Length of a Cube Given the Surface Area

question.text: The surface area of a cube is $150$ square units. Find the length of the edges of the cube.
question.explanation:
The surface area $S$ of a cube is made up of $6$ congruent squares. So, the area $\mathcal A$ of one face is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac{S}{6} = \dfrac{150}{6} = 25\,. \]

Since $\mathcal A = s^2,$ where $s$ is the length of an edge, we can find $s$ as follows: \[ s = \sqrt{\mathcal{A}} = \sqrt{25} = 5 \]

Therefore, the length of the edges is $5$ units.

example.title: Finding the Side Length of a Cube Given the Surface Area

question.text: The surface area of a cube is $294\,\textrm{cm}^2.$ Find the length of the edges of the cube.
question.explanation:
The surface area $S$ of a cube is made up of $6$ congruent squares. So, the area $\mathcal A$ of one face is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac{S}{6} = \dfrac{294}{6} = 49\,\textrm{cm}^2\,. \]

Since $\mathcal A = s^2,$ where $s$ is the length of an edge, we can find $s$ as follows: \[ s = \sqrt{\mathcal{A}} = \sqrt{49} = 7\,\textrm{cm} \]

Therefore, the length of the edges is $7\,\textrm{cm}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Lateral Surface Area of a Cube Given its Dimensions

question.text: Determine the lateral surface area for the cube above.
question.explanation:
The lateral surface area $S_L$ of a cube can be found using the formula

\[ S_L = 4s^2, \]

where $s$ is the side length of the cube.

Substituting $s = 3\sqrt 5\,\textrm{cm}$ into the formula, we get \[ S_L = 4(3\sqrt 5\, \text{cm})^2 = 180 \,\textrm{cm}^2. \]

example.title: Calculating the Lateral Surface Area of a Cube Given its Dimensions

question.text: The lateral surface area of a cube is $400\,\textrm{ft}^2.$ Find the length of the edges of the cube.
question.explanation:
The lateral surface area $S_L$ of a cube is made up of $4$ congruent squares. So, the area $\mathcal A$ of one face is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac{S_L}{4} = \dfrac{400}{4} = 100\,\textrm{ft}^2\,. \]

Since $\mathcal A = s^2,$ where $s$ is the length of an edge, we can find $s$ as follows: \[ s = \sqrt{\mathcal{A}} = \sqrt{100} = 10 \,\textrm{ft} \]

Therefore, the length of the edges is $10 \,\textrm{ft}.$
